transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

My mind just won’t shut off about work and everything else, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off no matter what I do. It feels like I’m stuck in this nonstop loop of “what ifs,” and it’s starting to affect how I function day to day. I’d really like help finding a way to quiet my mind so I’m not constantly on edge.
How long have you been feeling this constant worrying and being on edge—would you say it’s been more than six months, or more like days to a few weeks after a specific stressful event?

It’s been going on for about nine months now, pretty much since I took that promotion and became the main bilingual contact for a big client. So definitely more than six months, not just a few weeks after one thing.

Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling mostly sad or down and losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or is it more that you feel tense and worried but your mood is otherwise okay when you’re not thinking about your worries?

It’s more that I feel tense and worried all the time rather than mainly sad. I’ve been skipping dance nights and hikes and canceling plans, but that’s mostly because I feel too drained and anxious or stuck thinking about work, not because I don’t like those things anymore.

When you’re in this constant worry mode, do you also notice physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, feeling keyed up, trouble concentrating, irritability, or trouble falling or staying asleep—and if so, which of these are happening for you most days?

Yeah, I definitely notice several of those most days. I feel really keyed up and tense a lot—my shoulders are tight and I’m always tapping my foot—and I have a hard time falling asleep and staying asleep, so I wake up feeling unrested. My concentration is also pretty bad lately; my mind goes blank or keeps drifting when I’m trying to focus on work.
When your worrying starts, do you feel like you can control or put it aside if you really try, or does it feel excessive and very hard to stop even when you know it’s not helpful?

It feels really excessive and like I can’t stop it, even when I’m telling myself it’s not logical or helpful. Once a worry starts, it just spirals into worst‑case scenarios, and trying to distract myself or reason with it doesn’t really switch it off—it just keeps running in the background.

Do you ever have sudden, intense episodes of fear or discomfort that peak within minutes—like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like you might lose control or die—or is your anxiety more of a constant, slow-burning worry throughout the day without those sharp spikes?

It’s much more of a constant, slow‑burning worry throughout the day. I feel wired and on edge a lot, but I don’t really get those sudden, intense episodes where I think I’m going to die or completely lose control.

Are your worries mainly focused on work and this promotion, or do you also find yourself excessively worrying about many other areas of life like health, family, finances, or everyday things even when there’s no clear problem?

It started with work and the promotion, but now it’s spread to pretty much everything. I worry a lot about messing up scripts for this big client, saying something wrong when I’m mentoring, my parents’ health, and my student loans—even when nothing specific is actually wrong, my brain jumps to worst‑case scenarios in all those areas.

How much are these worries and physical symptoms getting in the way of your daily life—for example at work, in your relationships, or in taking care of yourself—and do they feel distressing enough that you wish they would stop or be much less intense?

They’re getting in the way a lot—I’ve started missing project deadlines and zoning out in client meetings because I’m so anxious and unfocused. I cancel plans with friends and skip dance or hikes because I feel too drained and wired, and the poor sleep makes everything harder. It’s really distressing, and I definitely wish the worrying and tension would just stop or at least be way less intense.

Do you ever feel a strong urge to do certain repetitive actions or mental rituals—like checking, counting, or repeating things—to try to prevent something bad from happening or to neutralize your worries, or is it mostly just the worrying itself without any rituals like that?

It’s mostly just the worrying itself without specific rituals. My mind runs through worst‑case scenarios and replays emails or possible escalations, but I don’t have set behaviors like counting, checking things in a certain order, or repeating phrases to make the anxiety go away.

Do you feel that your anxiety is mainly a reaction to this specific promotion and work situation and would likely ease a lot if that changed, or does this kind of excessive worrying feel like it’s been a long‑standing pattern for you even across different life situations?

I think the intensity it’s at now really ramped up with this promotion and being the main contact for that client about nine months ago. I’ve always been a bit of a “worrier,” even back in school, but this level of constant, excessive worrying that bleeds into everything and messes with my sleep and work feels new since this job change.
